challenge.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to .faff/ at all, not only committing them; caching resolved API keys in .faff/cache/credentials.json writes literal secrets to disk under .faff/, which is exactly what the guardrail prohibits. Gitignore only prevents commits; it does not stop the file being read by other processes, swept into backups, logs or artifact uploads, or leaked by a later tool that globs .faff/. The claimed benefit (re-reading process.env per call) is negligible next to an LLM network call and is unmeasured in the argument, and an in-memory cache per session would get the same benefit without persisting secrets. Calling it 'no behaviour change' ignores the new at-rest secret exposure.
